core_obligations: Reduce to affine S and X and write the strict transform as a quotient by a-power torsion (proof lines 8881-8889).
Show the a-power torsion vanishes at primes not containing a and at primes containing a using flatness (proof lines 8889-8901).
Conclude globally by the local criterion (proof lines 8902-8905).
difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma, two assertions: if X is flat over S at all points lying over Z then the strict transform of X is the base change X x_S S', and if a quasi-coherent F is flat over S at all points lying over Z then its strict transform is the pullback pr_X^*F (source lines 8868-8879). The proof of part (2) - which implies part (1) by definition of the strict transform of a scheme - localises to Spec(A) and Spec(B), writes the strict transform as N' = (N (x)_A A[I/a]) / a-power-torsion, and shows the a-power torsion of N (x)_A A[I/a] vanishes: at a prime not containing a the element maps to zero by construction, at a prime containing a flatness of N_q over A removes the torsion, and Algebra's local criterion makes y zero globally.
